content: The Trump administration has been including orders for Boeing Co. planes in trade discussions, and that’s helping to restore Bank of America Corp.’s confidence in the stock.

title: The US Economy Has a Leak
content: Hello and welcome to the newsletter, a grab bag of daily content from the Odd Lots universe. Sometimes it's us, Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway, bringing you our thoughts on the most recent developments in markets, finance and the economy. And sometimes it's contributions from our network of expert guests and sources. Whatever it is, we promise it will always be interesting.

title: Treasuries Fall as Tariff Concerns Cloud Outlook, ISM Weaker
content: Treasuries remained lower amid broad weakness in US assets on Monday, as worries over President Donald Trump’s tariff policy swirl at the start of a busy week for data on the health of the world’s largest economy.

title: Wall Street Sees Deeper Rout as Dollar Nears 2023 Low
content: Wall Street banks are reinforcing their calls that the dollar will weaken further, hit by interest-rate cuts, slowing economic growth and President Donald Trump’s trade and tax policies.

title: Alberta Wildfires Shut Down About 7% of Canada’s Oil Production
content: Wildfires in Canada’s energy heartland of Alberta have shut down almost 350,000 barrels of daily heavy crude production — about 7% of the country’s output — as a major blaze near the province’s eastern border menaces oil sands operations.

title: US Stocks Slip as Trade Friction, Weak Data Dent Sentiment
content: US equities edged lower Monday as reemerging tensions around global trade and a weak manufacturing report sapped investor confidence.

title: The Ratings Underdog Making Waves in Private Credit
content: Egan-Jones is a small but significant player in the private credit market,  grading over three thousand investments last year with a team of just 20 analysts. The firm's fast growth and optimistic ratings, however, are raising concerns about the risks in the private credit market, with some major investors excluding them from their lists of acceptable credit graders. Bloomberg Private Credit Reporter Silas Brown joined Wall Street Beat on Bloomberg Open Interest with the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Surges With Rising Global Tensions Boosting Haven Demand
content: Gold surged on revived demand for safer assets as the US and China traded accusations, while a dramatic series of attacks clouded the prospects of peace between Russia and Ukraine.

title: Bloomberg Surveillance 6/2/2025
content: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Diamond Wars: The Future of Lab Grown vs. Natural Diamonds
content: Lab Grown diamonds continue to put pressure on the $370 billion dollar global jewelry market. For the first time ever, more than half of engagement rings are made with lab grown diamonds. Despite the boom, De Beers says it will be closing its lab-grown diamond jewelry brand Lightbox. Ankur Daga, the Co-Founder and CEO of Angara, an online jeweler. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Some Retailers Can Get Away With Raising Prices, Widlitz Says
content: Stacey Widlitz, SW Retail Advisors president, says many consumers are still willing to pay higher prices, despite tariffs. She says many brands are getting away with raising prices if their products are in demand. She is on "Bloomberg Surveillance" talking about the impact of tariffs on retailers and says there could be fewer deals for customers in the electronic and footwear space. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: German Banks Pay Millions to Settle Claims by Insolvent Signa
content: Helaba and other German lenders have paid millions of euros in recent weeks to settle claims by the administrator of former real estate tycoon Rene Benko’s Signa Prime Selection AG.

title: Mali Court Postpones Ruling on Barrick Gold Mine to June 5
content: A Malian court has for the third time postponed a ruling on whether Barrick Gold Corp.’s Loulo-Gounkoto mine should be placed under state administration.

title: Eramet Drops as Gabon Aims to End Manganese Ore Exports
content: Eramet SA shares fell as much as 5.7% after Gabon decided to ban the export of manganese ore from 2029, jeopardizing the French miner’s biggest source of profit.

title: Trump Wants to Sell 1 Million Barrel Reserve of Diesel Fuel
content: The Trump administration wants to put a 1 million barrel cache of diesel fuel on the market, saying the reserve meant to provide an emergency supply of home heating oil for the Northeast has never been used for its intended purpose.

title: Saylor’s Bitcoin Copycats Fall Behind as Speculative Pop Fizzles
content: Turns out, buying Bitcoin to boost your share price might not be the corporate panacea that it once seemed.

title: US Manufacturing Contracts for a Third Month
content: The Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing index edged down 0.2 point last month to 48.5. The ISM’s import measure dropped 7.2 points, one of the largest monthly slides on record, to 39.9. Mike McKee reports on “Bloomberg Open Interest.” (Corrects to show third month of contraction)

title: Circle, Backers Seek $896 Million After Boosting IPO Size
content: Circle Internet Group Inc. and its shareholders have increased the size and price of the company’s initial public offering, suggesting strong investor demand for the stock.

title: Oil Advances as OPEC+ Supply Boost Vies With Geopolitical Risk
content: Oil surged after OPEC+ increased production less than some had feared and geopolitical concerns flared in Ukraine and Iran.

title: US Aluminum and Steel Prices Surge as Trump Doubles Tariffs
content: Futures tracking aluminum and steel prices in the US surged after President Donald Trump said he will double tariffs on the metals this week.

title: Bristol-Myers to Pay $11 Billion to License Cancer Drug
content: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. will pay BioNTech SE as much as $11.1 billion to license a next-generation cancer drug, as competition intensifies in an area of oncology that seeks to harness the immune system to attack tumors. Bloomberg's Damian Garde reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can Starz Break into Hollywood's Big League?
content: Starz is fresh off its separation from Lionsgate and it's betting it can take on the likes of Netflix and HBO. The entertainment company added 530,000 streaming customers in the fourth quarter. STARZ President and CEO Jeffrey Hirsch joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how he plans on transforming the company into a production powerhouse. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Quant Hedge Fund CFM Eyes Canada Expansion With Toronto Office
content: French quantitative hedge fund Capital Fund Management SA opened an office in Toronto to attract wealthy investors in Canada.

title: Matthei Gives Chile Vote Pledges a Reality Check on Fiscal Woes
content: Faced with an electoral campaign fought on two fronts — against the left and the hard right — Chile’s presidential front-runner Evelyn Matthei is trying to mark a difference not through sweeping promises, but by recognizing the cold, hard facts of a weak economy.

title: Revved-Up Polish Assets Dip as Election Erodes Pro-EU Tilt
content: Polish stocks and bonds — among the world’s stand-out performers of 2025 — dipped after a nationalist unexpectedly won the presidential election, dealing a blow to the government.

title: Suspect in Colorado Attack Criminally Charged by US Prosecutors
content: The man arrested over an attack at an event in support of Israeli hostages in Gaza that left at least eight injured was criminally charged by US prosecutors in Colorado.

title: From AI to Nukes: Here’s What’s in the UK’s Big Defense Overhaul
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s government outlined a new defense strategy on Monday that aims to put a “stronger, more lethal” North Atlantic Treaty Organization at the forefront of British defense plans as the country boosts its nuclear deterrent, rebuilds munitions and weapons stockpiles and invests billions of pounds into technologically-advanced warfare methods.

title: Trump Plans to Tap Biden’s Green Bank to Make Billions in Loans
content: The Trump administration plans to use a $400 billion green bank the president once sought to kill to finance billions of dollars in loans for nuclear reactors, geothermal power and critical minerals, according to details of the administration’s fiscal year 2026 budget request.

title: Trump Condemns Boulder Attack, Blames Lax Immigration Policies
content: President Donald Trump condemned an attack in Boulder, Colorado that targeted a march in support of Israeli hostages held by Hamas and said he would work to remove the suspect in the attack from the US.

title: Starmer Seeks Nuclear Build-Up in Sweeping UK Military Revamp
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer backed a sweeping overhaul of the British military yet refused to commit to the full extent of spending increases that experts said is necessary to protect the UK from growing global threats.

title: Mexico Judicial Election Sees 13% Turnout in Historic Vote
content: The future of Mexico’s judiciary was decided by a small minority of voters after an unprecedented election of federal judges, including all members of the nation’s top court.

title: EU Votes to Curb China’s Access to Medical Device Procurement
content: The European Union agreed overwhelmingly to curb Chinese medical device manufacturers’ access to public procurement contracts in the bloc, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Russia and Ukraine Agree on New Prisoner Swap But Fail to Reach Truce
content: Russia and Ukraine wrapped up a second round of talks in Istanbul that failed to bring the two sides closer to ending the war, but laid the groundwork for a new exchange of prisoners.

title: Ukraine’s Brazen Drone Strike on Nuclear Bombers Alarms Moscow
content: Ukraine’s drone strike deep inside Russian territory left Kremlin officials angry and alarmed over the sudden vulnerability of a nuclear-capable air fleet far from the battlefield, according to people close to senior officials in Moscow.

content: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are likely to speak this week, according to a Trump administration official, as the world’s two largest economies remain locked in trade turmoil.

content: A divided US Supreme Court declined to consider a new expansion of constitutional gun rights, turning away challenges to a Maryland ban on so-called assault weapons and a Rhode Island prohibition on high-capacity magazines.

title: EU Warns It Could Accelerate Retaliatory Tariffs Over US Duties
content: The European Union is preparing for another round of trade talks with the US and warned that it may speed up retaliatory measures if President Donald Trump follows through on his tariff threats, the latest of which includes a 50% levy on steel and aluminum imports.

title: Russia and Ukraine Conclude Talks After Kyiv Hits Bombers
content: Russia and Ukraine wrapped up their latest direct peace talks in Istanbul a day after Kyiv staged one of its boldest aerial attacks inside Russia, destroying long-range bombers and other aircraft.

title: Philippines Aims to Cut Reliance on Vietnam for Rice
content: The Philippines, the world’s top rice importer, plans to look beyond its dominant supplier, Vietnam, to ensure steady supplies and competitive prices at home.

title: Nationalist Wins Poland’s Presidency in Setback for EU Ties
content: A nationalist candidate backed by Donald Trump won Poland’s presidential election, defeating the centrist mayor of Warsaw and complicating efforts to shift the nation back into the European Union mainstream.

title: Ukraine Building Drone Hunters as Fight Moves Far Beyond Front
content: A battle is shaping up in the skies over Ukraine and Russia, as the ingenuity of drone engineers on both sides opens up new opportunities and threats far behind the front lines.

title: MAGA-Backed Win in Poland Sends Europe a Warning
content: The revenge of “places that don’t matter” is increasingly palpable from Portugal to Poland.

title: Emirates Reviews Russia Flights as Ukraine Expands Drone Use
content: The world’s largest long-haul carrier plans to review flights to Russia following Ukrainian drone attacks deep inside the country over the weekend.

title: Polish Boxer-Turned-President Set for Showdown With Government
content: Karol Nawrocki has made a career out of fighting. An amateur boxing champion and self-confessed football hooligan, the historian-turned-politician has written books on anti-communist groups and organized crime.

title: Reeves Says Tories Cost UK Taxpayer £1.4 Billion in Failed Covid Contracts
content: Deficient pandemic-era contracts for protective equipment cost the British taxpayer £1.4 billion ($1.9 billion), the UK’s Labour government said on Monday, blaming the former Conservative administration for “reckless handling” of public money.

title: Amazon Hit by German Warning Over Price Controls on Marketplace
content: Amazon.com Inc. was warned by Germany’s antitrust watchdog that price controls for retailers on its marketplace are likely to violate national and European Union laws.

title: Romania Injects More Funds to Banks as Market Shortage Narrows
content: Romania’s central bank injected liquidity into domestic banks for a second week as it sought to further calm money markets after increased volatility during recent political turmoil.

title: MAGA Triumphs in Poland’s Presidential Election
content: Welcome to Balance of Power, bringing you the latest in global politics. If you haven’t yet, sign up here.

title: Senate Begins Putting Its Stamp on Giant Trump Tax, Debt Limit Bill
content: Significant changes are in store for President Donald Trump’s signature $3.9 trillion tax-cut bill as the Senate begins closed-door talks this week on legislation that squeaked through the House by a single vote.

title: Trump Plans to Offload National Park Sites, But States Don’t Want Them
content: The White House wants to trim the National Park Service budget by transferring some parks to state and tribal management. States say their resources are already tight.

title: Bolsonaro’s Plan to Stage a Trumpian Comeback Might Save Lula’s Presidency
content: Jair Bolsonaro’s insistence he can pull off a Donald Trump-like comeback in Brazil’s looming election has paralyzed his fervent right-wing movement, effectively blocking the search for a successor to the ineligible former president.

title: Tesla Sales Plunge to an Almost Three-Year Low in France
content: Tesla Inc.’s new-vehicle registrations fell further in France, undercutting Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk’s assertion last month that the carmaker has recovered from its early-year sales slump. Bloomberg's Craig Trudell reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

content: Campbell’s Co.’s organic sales returned to growth last quarter as penny-pinching consumers opted to eat in more.

content: McKinsey & Co.’s consultants are increasingly drafting proposals and making PowerPoint slides using the firm’s generative artificial intelligence platform, which has developed enough to take over at least some of the tasks typically performed by junior employees.

title: Telkom Indonesia Is Said to Weigh Sale of Health-Care Firm AdMedika
content: PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia is considering selling AdMedika and seeking at least $100 million for the health-care firm, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Atos Gets Offer From French State for Strategic Computing Assets
content: Atos SE said it received an offer from the French state for the group’s advanced computing assets, which values the unit deemed critical to the country’s nuclear industry at €410 million ($467 million).

title: Tom Cruise’s Final ‘Mission Impossible’ Tops China Box Office
content: Tom Cruise’s film is back on top in China. Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning posted the biggest opening for a US film in the country this year, defying trade and geopolitical tensions between Washington and Beijing.

title: Ads Ruined Social Media. Now They’re Coming to AI.
content: Chatbots are pivoting to the ad model and optimizing for eyeballs, just like social media did. Remember how that turned out?

title: Nintendo Has a Shrewd Plan for Selling the Switch 2 in Japan
content: Nintendo Co. is making an unusual move with its Switch 2 distribution in Japan: It’s setting wholesale prices so retailers can earn more from each sale.

title: Southeast Asia Joins Europe’s Calls to Defend Subsea Cables
content: Defense officials from Europe and Southeast Asia called for stronger collaboration to protect the global network of subsea cables as concerns grow over threats to this vital infrastructure.

title: Samsung Nears Wide-Ranging Deal With Perplexity for AI Features
content: Samsung Electronics Co. is nearing a wide-ranging deal to invest in Perplexity AI Inc. and put search technology from the artificial intelligence startup at the forefront of the South Korean company’s devices.

title: Apple Developer Event Will Show It’s Still Far From Being an AI Leader
content: Apple, a year after debuting its AI platform, will do little at WWDC to show it’s catching up to leaders like OpenAI and Google. Also: The latest macOS gets its new California theme; a look at why the company is moving to an iOS 26 and macOS 26 naming system; and details on Apple’s dedicated gaming app.

title: Chile’s Economic Growth Triples Forecast as Mining Surges
content: Chile’s economy grew more than expected in April as mining output jumped, offsetting a drop in manufacturing and retail, according to the central bank’s main gauge of monthly activity.

content: The Philippines, the world’s top rice importer, plans to look beyond its dominant supplier, Vietnam, to ensure steady supplies and competitive prices at home.

content: Romania’s central bank injected liquidity into domestic banks for a second week as it sought to further calm money markets after increased volatility during recent political turmoil.

title: Risks Abound If Trump Ties Tariffs to a Balance-of-Payments Crisis
content: Countries tend to avoid declaring they’re facing balance-of-payments problems, for good reason. They unnerve markets. They remind people of policy failures in places like Argentina, Greece or Thailand. They conjure up images of IMF technocrats flying in to enforce austerity regimes.

title: It’s Not Just Trump Vs Harvard as Global Universities Turn Inward

title: Chile’s Long Road to CPI Target Sees Peso Bonds Back in Favor
content: Investors are exiting Chilean inflation-linked bonds in favor of instruments denominated in pesos on confidence that CPI is on track to hit the target in early 2026 for the first time in more than five years.

title: Carney Aims to Thwart Trump’s Tariff Assault by Unlocking Internal Trade
content: Prime Minister Mark Carney is pushing to offset the economic pain caused by US President Donald Trump’s tariffs by compelling Canadian provinces to liberalize trade with one another.

title: UK House Prices Post Surprise Increase in May, Nationwide Says
content: UK house prices unexpectedly rose in May, in a sign that demand for housing remains resilient following the expiry of a tax break for buyers, according to one of Britain’s largest mortgage lenders.

title: Putin’s Central Banker Under Fire to Cut Record-High Rates
content: The Bank of Russia’s governor, who was praised for helping save the country’s economy after the invasion of Ukraine, is facing mounting pressure to reverse course on record-high borrowing costs amid worries over their toll on business.

title: Japan to Seek $840 Billion of Inward Foreign Investment by 2030
content: Japan plans to raise its incoming foreign direct investment target to ¥120 trillion ($840 billion) by 2030, aiming to attract more overseas capital to help revitalize struggling regional economies and address labor shortages.

title: Madagascar Courts UAE Investment to Offset US Tariff Threat
content: Madagascar is seeking to boost investments from the United Arab Emirates to spur growth in its tourism and energy sectors, a partnership that’s become more urgent as its faces steep tariffs from the US.

title: Swiss Growth Revised Up on Export Surge Before Trump Tariffs
content: Switzerland’s growth spurt into 2025 was even more pronounced than initially estimated, with the economy expanding at the fastest pace in two years.

title: Swedish Bankruptcy Rate Edges Higher in May Amid Consumer Gloom
content: The number of bankruptcies in Sweden continues to tick higher as the uncertainty surrounding tariffs weighs on consumers’ willingness to spend.

title: Hong Kong’s 2025 Growth Outlook Cut by AMRO on Trade Uncertainty
content: Hong Kong’s growth outlook was cut by a regional organization, which urged the city to diversify its economy and trading partners to counter growing protectionism.

title: ECB Set for Last Easy Rate Cut as Trade Fuels Inflation Discord
content: The European Central Bank is about to lower interest rates for the final time before an increasingly complicated inflation outlook risks bringing internal divisions to the fore.

title: Japan to Set Up Minister-Level Meeting to Address Rice Supplies
content: Japan will set up a minister-level meeting as early as this week to address the supply of rice, Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba said in parliament on Monday, as the government seeks to stabilize the price of the nation’s staple grain and quell public anger ahead of a summer election.

title: BOK’s Rhee Says US-China Trade Talks Important for Asia
content: Bank of Korea Governor Rhee Chang-yong said the outcome of trade negotiations between the US and China will have an impact on all of Asia’s economies, highlighting their significance beyond the bilateral level.

title: China Accuses US of Violating Trade Deal, Vows Firm Response
content: China accused the US of violating their recent trade deal and vowed to take measures to defend its interests, dimming the prospect of an immediate leadership call that Donald Trump wants to have to further bilateral talks.

title: Japan’s Akazawa Reportedly Mulls Return to US This Week
content: Japan’s top trade negotiator Ryosei Akazawa is considering returning to the US for another round of trade negotiations this week as expectations mount for a deal as early as this month.

title: Trade War Hits Asia Factories as Exports, Production Slide
content: Manufacturing activity across several Asian nations weakened in May as US tariffs and trade uncertainty eroded demand.

title: Fed’s Waller Outlines Path to Rate Cuts Later This Year
content: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he continues to see a path to interest-rate cuts later this year amid his expectations that tariffs will boost unemployment and temporarily increase inflation.

title: Stephen Roach Now Says It’s Too Early to Declare Hong Kong Over
content: Stephen Roach is revising his declaration that Hong Kong is finished.

title: Japan’s Firms Raised Capital Spending Ahead of US Tariffs
content: Japanese businesses increased capital investment at a faster pace in the first quarter of this year just as the Trump administration touted the coming tariff campaign that kicked off in March.

title: UK Non-Dom Exits Seen Hitting at Least 10%, With More to Come
content: At least 10% of the UK’s wealthy non-dom population have left the country following tighter tax rules introduced by Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s Labour government, according to a new report authored by a former Treasury economist.

title: South Korea’s Election Frontrunner Still Leaves Many Unconvinced
content: Lee Jae-myung is still the frontrunner in South Korea’s presidential race, but what once looked like a landslide victory has turned into a much closer contest.

title: Pro-EU Mayor Takes Slim Lead in Poland Vote, Exit Polls Show
content: The centrist mayor of Warsaw took a slim lead in Poland’s presidential election over a nationalist candidate backed by Donald Trump, giving a boost to the country’s pro-European Union government, exit polls show.

title: Group That Won Trump Trade Ruling Wants Tariffs Halted During Appeal
content: A group of small businesses who won a ruling that most of President Donald Trump’s global tariffs are illegal want them blocked during the administration’s appeal, saying they were suffering immediate harm from economic uncertainty.

title: Marc Maron Quits Podcasting After 16-Year Run, Citing Burnout
content: Marc Maron’s long-running podcast WTF with Marc Maron will air its final episode this fall, the comedian announced Monday, ending a pioneering 16-year run that helped define the podcast medium.

title: Boeing Upgraded to Buy at Bank of America as Trump Favors Planemaker for Trade Talks
content: The Trump administration has been including orders for Boeing Co. planes in trade discussions, and that’s helping to restore Bank of America Corp.’s confidence in the stock.

title: UnitedHealth Investors Back CEO’s $60 Million Pay Package
content: UnitedHealth Group Inc. shareholders approved a pay package for Chief Executive Officer Stephen Hemsley that includes a $60 million stock option award.

title: Alberta Wildfires Shut Down About 7% of Canada’s Oil Production
content: Wildfires in Canada’s energy heartland of Alberta have shut down almost 350,000 barrels of daily heavy crude production — about 7% of the country’s output — as a major blaze near the province’s eastern border menaces oil sands operations.

title: Byron Allen Hires Moelis to Shop $1 Billion in Local TV Stations
content: Producer and host Byron Allen has hired Moelis & Co. to find buyers for 28 local TV stations his company owns, in an effort to reduce debt while taking advantage of potential deregulation in the broadcast business.

title: Daiwa Pauses M&A Hiring as Tariff Uncertainty Chokes Deal Flow
content: Daiwa Securities Group Inc. boss Akihiko Ogino said the Japan brokerage won’t be pushing to add staff working on mergers and acquisitions, providing a downbeat assessment on the impact to dealmaking from US President Donald Trump’s trade policy.

title: Flagship India EV Policy to Be a ‘Non-Starter’ for Global Giants
content: India is rolling out a new flagship electric vehicle policy that aims to lure global automakers into making cars locally. It knows Tesla Inc. may still not bite.

title: Supreme Court Lets Finra Case Proceed in Test of Wall Street’s Self Regulation
content: The US Supreme Court let the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority proceed with disciplinary proceedings against a brokerage accused of stealing from customers in a case testing Wall Street’s longstanding reliance on self-regulatory organizations.

title: Philippines Aims to Cut Reliance on Vietnam for Rice
content: The Philippines, the world’s top rice importer, plans to look beyond its dominant supplier, Vietnam, to ensure steady supplies and competitive prices at home.

title: New World’s Distress Worsens After Delay on Bond Interest
content: Hong Kong developer New World Development Co. is sliding deeper into distress after jolting investors by delaying interest payments on some bonds, marking the latest flashpoint in a years-long crisis in China’s property market.

title: Dimon Says His Retirement From JPMorgan Is ‘Several Years Away’
content: Jamie Dimon said his retirement from the top post at JPMorgan Chase & Co. is “several years away,” but the decision is up to the bank’s directors.

title: Breast Cancer Growth Slowed by 14 Months in New AstraZeneca Drug Study
content: AstraZeneca Plc and Daiichi Sankyo Co.’s Enhertu delayed the advance of a common type of breast cancer by more than a year in a large study, a result that may lead to expanded use of the medicine.

title: Neuralink Rival Paradromics Tests Brain Implant in First Human
content: Paradromics Inc., a brain implant company and rival to Elon Musk’s Neuralink, tested its device in its first human patient last month.

title: Chime, Holders Seek $832 Million in IPO at Reduced Valuation
content: Chime Financial Inc. and some of its shareholders are seeking to raise as much as $832 million from an initial public offering, which could give the San Francisco-based fintech a fully diluted valuation of as much as roughly $11 billion, a significant drop from its peak valuation in 2021.

title: Leela Luxury Hotels Owner’s India IPO Gets Off to a Tepid Start
content: The shares of the operator of the India’s Leela luxury hotels made a lackluster debut in Mumbai after having raised money through India’s second-largest initial public offering this year.

title: Deutsche Bank Hires Veteran HSBC Telecom Banker Bailey
content: Deutsche Bank AG is hiring veteran HSBC Holdings Plc telecom banker Dan Bailey, people with knowledge of the matter said.

title: Tesla Sales Plunge 67% to an Almost Three-Year Low in France
content: Tesla Inc.’s new-vehicle registrations fell further in France, undercutting Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk’s assertion last month that the carmaker has recovered from its early-year sales slump.

title: Monzo Profit Soars as British Challenger Bank Boosts Lending
content: Monzo Bank Ltd. said its profit quadrupled last year with a burgeoning loan book and customer growth lifting revenue, as the mobile bank works toward an eventual stock market debut.

title: PwC Troubles in China Deepen With Exit of Hong Kong Partners
content: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP troubles are now deepening in Hong Kong as the firm is wrestling with the consequences of its audits of China Evergrande Group.

title: TDB Warns Losses on African Development Banks Set Dangerous Precedent
content: Forcing African development lenders to take losses in sovereign debt restructurings would set a dangerous precedent and increase the cost of financing on the continent, TDB President and Managing Director Admassu Tadesse cautioned.

title: Sanofi to Buy Immunology Biotech Blueprint for $9.1 Billion
content: Sanofi agreed to buy Blueprint Medicines Corp. for at least $9.1 billion as the French drugmaker expands further in rare immunological diseases.

title: BYD Shares Sink as Carmaker Faces Backlash Over EV Price War
content: BYD Co. shares fell, bringing losses over the past week to more than 17%, on concern that its price cuts are drawing government scrutiny and becoming unsustainable for the Chinese EV industry.

title: British Airways Owner Sees Transatlantic Slowdown Recovering
content: IAG SA said the weaker demand on transatlantic routes has shown signs of easing over the past three weeks as the travel outlook begins to stabilize following a period of uncertainty.

title: Tom Cruise’s Final ‘Mission Impossible’ Tops China Box Office
content: Tom Cruise’s film is back on top in China. Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning posted the biggest opening for a US film in the country this year, defying trade and geopolitical tensions between Washington and Beijing.

title: Air India CEO Says Pakistan Airspace Ban Adding to Flying Costs
content: The continuing ban for Indian airlines in using Pakistani airspace is adding flying hours for non-stop flights and will weigh down Air India Ltd.’s path to profitability, its top executive said in an interview.

title: Paraguay Pitches Argentina, Brazil on Natural Gas Pipeline Plan

title: Bank of Ghana Plans to Cap Non-Performing Loan Ratio at 10% by December 2026

From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg: The Asia Trade 06/05/2025
content: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Paul Allen and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wealth Manager: Chinese Investors Look to Diversify
content: Grant Pan, Noah Holdings CFO and ARK Hong Kong CEO, says wealthy Chinese investors have become more sophisticated. Pan says clients are now looking at markets such as Japan, Singapore and Europe to diversify. It's a change from high net worth individuals who were previously more focused on China and the US. He discusses this trend with Yvonne Man and Annabelle Droulers on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Former Australian Prime Minister Turnbull on Chinese Ownership of Darwin Port
content: Former Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull discusses Chinese ownership of the Port of Darwin in an interview with Bloomberg Television. Turnbull says "our assessment at the time was that this wasn't a security issue," but adds that the shifting geopolitical landscape means "there's a discomfort about a Chinese company owning port facilities" in the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ECB to Cut Rates as Trade Mess Weighs on the Economy
content: The European Central Bank is set to lower interest rates for an eighth time as President Donald Trump’s jolts to global trade dim the prospects for inflation and the economy.

title: Oil Investments to Fall 6% on Lower Demand and Prices, IEA Says
content: Global oil investments are expected to drop 6% in 2025, in the first such decline in a decade excluding the year of the Covid slump, according to the International Energy Agency.

title: Neuberger Berman Raises $4 Billion for New Secondary Fund
content: Neuberger Berman has raised more than $4 billion for its latest general partner-led secondary fund despite a challenging environment for private capital fundraising.

title: This Might Be the ‘Biggest Year’ in Tech: Bosworth
content: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth speaks at Bloomberg Tech San Francisco 2025 about why this year could be pivotal for the development of the metaverse, highlighting unique opportunities emerging for engineers across the tech industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan’s Bonds Back on Stage With Another Sale of Longer Debt
content: Japan’s sovereign debt is back in the spotlight as the government prepares for another sale of super-long-term bonds after dismal showings at recent auctions, as demand for the far-end of the curve sputters across the globe.

title: President Trump Signs Travel Ban for 12 Countries
content: President Donald Trump has signed a proclamation that bans individuals from 12 countries from entering the US. Bloomberg's John Harney reports on the latest from Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Meta CTO on What's Ahead in Artificial Intelligence / DAY 1
content: Andrew “Boz” Bosworth, Chief Technology Officer & Head of Reality Labs at Meta spoke about harnessing engineering talent and his leadership priorities at Meta, including what’s next for a hardware rollout in the AI era with Bloomberg’s Tom Giles at Bloomberg Tech in San Francisco. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Enterprise Products Says US Set to Deny Its China Ethane Export License
content: Enterprise Products Partners LP received a notice saying the US intends to deny licenses for three proposed cargoes of ethane heading to China as the Trump administration doubles down on security for exports to the country.

title: Glencore-Backed Cobalt Holdings Axes $230 Million London IPO
content: Cobalt Holdings Plc has decided not to proceed with its planned initial public offering in London.

title: Vietnam Sends Trade Demand Reply as US Turns Up China Heat
content: Vietnam said it is responding to US demands with “goodwill” and has sent a written reply to US trade requests after the Trump administration vowed to keep pressuring the Southeast Asian nation to reduce its role in China supply chains.

title: China Offers $1,400 Bounty for Arrests of Taiwan Cyberwarriors
content: China placed a bounty on cyberwarriors working for Taiwan’s Defense Ministry, extending its campaign to squeeze President Lai Ching-te.

title: Ex-Australia PM Says He Could Have Halted Port Lease to Chinese Firm
content: Former Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull said he could have halted the lease of the Port of Darwin to a Chinese company shortly after coming to power a decade ago — pulling the plug on a deal the US “never liked.”

title: Germany’s Got a Problem, and It’s More Than Donald Trump
content: As Donald Trump pushes ahead with his campaign to transform the way the world does business, Germany is uniquely vulnerable.

title: Elon Musk Urges Americans Take Action to ‘Kill’ Trump Tax Cut Bill
content: Elon Musk is on a mission to block President Donald Trump’s tax bill after he tried — and failed — to convince Republican lawmakers to preserve valuable tax credits for electric vehicles in the legislation, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Xi Tells Lukashenko China Will Hold Military Parade on Sept. 3
content: President Xi Jinping said China will hold a military parade to commemorate the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II on Sept. 3, an event that’s expected to bring his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to Beijing.

title: Trump Orders Inquiry Into Biden’s Health, Use of Autopen
content: President Donald Trump directed aides to investigate whether former President Joe Biden’s staff conspired to hide information about his health from the public and enacted any executive actions without his predecessor’s knowledge.

title: Trump Stymied in ‘Art of the Deal’ Approach to World’s Strongmen
content: President Donald Trump has long boasted about his ability to cut deals with the world’s strongmen. But now that he’s back in the White House, his charms haven’t worked on the leaders he professes to admire.

title: Trump Bars Foreign Students From Entering US to Attend Harvard
content: President Donald Trump signed an executive action that prevents foreign nationals from entering the US to study at Harvard University, accusing the school of failing to implement discipline on campus and fostering a dramatic rise in crime.

title: Kim Vows Full Backing for Putin as Ties With Russia Deepen
content: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un reiterated his pledge to unconditionally support Russian President Vladimir Putin, state media said, as the sanctions-defying alliance between the two countries raises security concerns in the region.

title: US to Keep Pressure on Vietnam Over China Imports, Lutnick Says
content: The Trump administration will keep up pressure on Vietnam as long as it keeps re-exporting a significant amount of Chinese products to the US, according to Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick.

title: The Rare-Earth Fight Imperiling US-China Trade Peace, Explained
content: Markets cheered in early May when the US and China agreed in Geneva to lower tariffs and other barriers. But after a few weeks, the shine started to come off that deal, with China accusing the US of violating it with new restrictions and the US saying China failed to honor promises on rare earths.

title: Hong Kong Bolsters Top Court With First Foreign Judge in a Year
content: Hong Kong has appointed a retired New Zealand judge to its top court, the first foreign justice named to the appellate body in over a year following record resignations that threatened to undermine confidence in the judicial system.

title: Senate GOP Plans to Boost CFPB Scrutiny, Cut Fed Employee Pay
content: The Senate Banking Committee is planning to eliminate all mandatory funding for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and restrict the pay of many Federal Reserve employees as part of the Senate’s big tax and spending bill, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Trump Signs Travel Ban for 12 Countries Including Afghanistan
content: President Donald Trump signed a proclamation that bans individuals from 12 countries from entering the US, reinstating one of the most controversial measures from his first term after an attack in Colorado that targeted an event supporting Israeli hostages.

title: Trump Violated Rights of Deported Venezuelans, Judge Rules
content: A US judge ruled that the Trump administration violated the due-process rights of more than 100 Venezuelans deported to a notorious prison in El Salvador, and they must now get a chance to challenge their removal.

title: Trump Broadcasts Putin Vow to Respond to Ukraine Attacks
content: Donald Trump on Wednesday broadcast Vladimir Putin’s warning that he’ll retaliate against Ukraine for its recent stunning drone strikes deep inside Russian territory, the clearest signal yet that the US president’s peace efforts have stalled.

title: Trump, GOP Senators Discussed Cutting SALT Break in Tax Bill
content: Donald Trump and Republican senators discussed ways to scale back the $40,000 state and local tax deduction cap in the House version of the president’s tax-cut bill, Senate Majority Leader John Thune said.

title: Trump’s Late-Night Lament Over Xi Deepens Impasse in Trade Fight
content: President Donald Trump is positioning a personal discussion with his Chinese counterpart as the key to preventing the world’s largest economies from spiraling deeper into their trade and technology fight.

title: Trump Officials Target Columbia Accreditation Over Pro-Palestine Protests
content: The Education Department said Columbia University no longer appeared to meet accreditation standards after concluding that the school is in violation of anti-discrimination laws, the latest effort by the Trump administration to target elite schools over their handling of pro-Palestinian protests.

title: Lutnick Says Hurricane Center’s Fully Staffed Despite Key Vacancies
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told a congressional committee that the US National Hurricane Center was fully staffed even though key positions are going unfilled as hurricane season begins.

title: Trump Budget Plan Raises Concern Over Cuts to Statistics Bureau
content: The Trump administration is proposing to cut resources from the Bureau of Labor Statistics when the agency is already reeling from years of budget constraints, further compounding concerns about the quality and quantity of data produced about the US economy.

content: The US’s top steel providers are racing to win exemptions from Donald Trump’s steel tariffs.

content: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government faces the possibility of collapse and early elections after his ultra-Orthodox coalition partners on Wednesday threatened to bolt, according to Israeli media.

title: Walmart Fires Workers, Reviews Permits Over Immigration Ruling
content: Walmart Inc. is informing stores across the country to begin identifying workers whose work authorization may be expiring after the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could revoke protections for hundreds of thousands of migrants.

title: Trump Gets a Tentative Win From CBO's New Tax and Tariff Estimates
content: The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office handed Republicans a major political talking point Wednesday, with projections that showed the possibility for President Donald Trump’s tariffs to bring in more federal revenue than will be lost by his giant tax-cut plan.

title: Carney Holds Back on Tariff Retaliation, Says US-Canada Talks Are Progressing
content: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada and the US are in “intensive” talks about the countries’ trade relationship, explaining his government’s decision not to respond yet to the Trump administration’s doubling of steel and aluminum tariffs.

title: USDA to Review Reports Following Delay of Latest Trade Outlook
content: The US Department of Agriculture is undergoing a review of non-statutory reports including a quarterly forecast on trade that pointed to a record farming deficit.

title: Nintendo’s Switch 2 Lures Fans to Biggest Gadget Launch in Years
content: Nintendo Co. fans from Tokyo to Manhattan stood in line for hours to be among the first to get a Switch 2, fueling one of the biggest global gadget debuts since the iPhone launches of yesteryear.

title: Alphabet CEO Expects to Keep Hiring Engineers as AI Advances
content: Alphabet Inc.’s Sundar Pichai said his company will keep expanding its engineering ranks at least into 2026, stressing human talent remains key even as Google’s parent ramps up AI investments.

title: Meta’s Push Into Defense Tech Reflects Cultural Shift, CTO Says
content: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Technology Officer Andrew Bosworth said that the “tides have turned” in Silicon Valley and made it more palatable for the tech industry to support the US military’s efforts.

title: 23andMe’s DNA Data Gets Boosted $305 Million Bid in New Auction
content: Bankrupt genetic analysis company 23andMe will hold a second auction for its cache of DNA data with an opening bid of $305 million from group lead by the company’s former chief executive officer, Anne Wojcicki.

title: IBM Said to Have Pursued Informatica Ahead of Salesforce Deal
content: International Business Machines Corp. pursued Informatica Inc. before Salesforce Inc. bought the software company for $8 billion last month, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Elon Musk’s AI Startup Set to Get Debt Backing From TPG
content: TPG Angelo Gordon is an anchor investor in a debt package for Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence startup, xAI Corp., according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Uber, DoorDash Settle Delivery Fee Cap Dispute With New York
content: DoorDash Inc., Grubhub Inc. and Uber Technologies Inc.’s Uber Eats are settling a 2021 lawsuit against New York City over a cap on fees the meal-delivery services can charge restaurants.

title: Nvidia Director Discloses Proposal to Sell $550 Million Position
content: Billionaire Nvidia Corp. director Mark Stevens unloaded more than 1 million shares of the chipmaker this week as the stock rebounds from a slow start to the year.

title: Japanese Space-Debris Firm Loses Half Its Value a Year After IPO
content: When Astroscale Holdings Inc. began trading in Tokyo a year ago, excitement over the Japanese space-debris pioneer was riding so high that the stock surged 62%, making it a billion-dollar company.

title: Deliveroo Launches Drone Food Delivery Service in Dublin
content: Deliveroo has launched an autonomous drone food delivery service in Dublin in partnership with Irish firm Manna Drones Inc.

title: Xiaohongshu Valuation Hits $26 Billion in Boost for Backer GSR
content: Xiaohongshu’s valuation surged to $26 billion in recent market transactions via a major fund, an unusually fast ascent that underscores how the Chinese social media phenom is making headway against TikTok in the US.

title: Apple Loses Bid to Pause Court Order on App Store Changes
content: Apple Inc. lost its request to pause a court order requiring it to let App Store developers steer users to the web to purchase in-app items without paying a commission.

title: Best Buy, GameStop Expect Rapid Sellout of Switch 2 Consoles
content: Best Buy Co. expects to sell out its allotment of Nintendo Co.’s new Switch 2 game consoles shortly after they become available for purchase at midnight.

title: Tesla FSD's Role in Crash, GlobalFoundries Ups US Spend | Bloomberg Technology 6/4/2025
content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss footage and details from late 2023 when a Tesla using what the company calls Full Self-Driving (FSD) was in a fatal crash. Plus, GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen talks about his company’s plans to spend $16 billion to boost chip production in New York and Vermont. And HPE CEO Antonio Neri explains why the company has reduced how much it expects tariffs to impact earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chinese Hacked US Telecom a Year Before Known Wireless Breaches
content: Corporate investigators found evidence that Chinese hackers broke into an American telecommunications company in the summer of 2023, indicating the country’s attackers penetrated the US communications system earlier than publicly known.

title: Planet Labs CEO Says Europe Demand Beating Outset of Ukraine War
content: Earth imaging company Planet Labs PBC’s profit beat expectations as Europe hikes defense spending in response to the United States pulling back from the continent.

title: Reddit Sues Anthropic, Says AI Company Exploited User Data
content: Reddit Inc. sued artificial intelligence firm Anthropic, saying it has used the social media company’s content without permission to train its AI models.

title: FCC Departures Gut Panel With Big Merger, Investigation Pending
content: Two members of the Federal Communications Commission announced they’ll depart this week, leaving the agency with three vacancies while it reviews a major media merger and investigates a wireless provider.

title: Cyber Investigators Examine Video of Alleged Hackers on a Jet
content: Marco Rubio, US secretary of state, during a Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs hearing in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, May 20, 2025. The hearing is reviewing the fiscal year 2026 budget request for the US Department of State. Photographer: Nathan Howard/Bloomberg

title: CrowdStrike Says DOJ, SEC Sent Inquiries on Firm Accounting
content: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. said US officials have asked for information related to the accounting of deals it’s made with some customers and said the cybersecurity firm is cooperating with the inquiry.

title: US Is Reworking Subsidy Awards to Chipmakers, Lutnick Says
content: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the Trump administration has been reworking agreements forged with semiconductor makers under the 2022 Chips Act to secure what he called better terms aimed at generating additional domestic investment.

title: Italy to Strengthen STMicro, Not Tear It Apart, Minister Says
content: Italy intends to strengthen embattled semiconductor company STMicroelectronics NV, a joint venture with France, Industry Minister Adolfo Urso said.

title: Organized Crime Phishing Took £47 Million From UK Coffers
content: Organized crime has extracted £47 million ($64 million) from the UK government in a phishing operation, His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs officials said Wednesday.The operation, which took place last year, involved mimicking taxpayer credentials and claiming payments from HMRC, Angela MacDonald, second permanent secretary and deputy chief executive, told Parliament’s Treasury Committee. The incident wasn’t a cyberattack and no data from taxpayers was taken, she said.

title: AI-Power Demand Leads Brokerage Snapper to Hire Team
content: Commodity brokerage Snapper Creek Energy has built a power team focused on rising volatility in electricity markets as artificial intelligence and extreme weather upend grids.

title: Samsung’s Galaxy S25 Edge Shows the Limits of Impressively Thin Phones
content: Review: The handset, one of several slim devices coming this year, skimps on battery life for the sake of a light design.

title: CrowdStrike Shares Drop After Sales Forecast Underwhelms
content: Shares of CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. fell after the cybersecurity company projected revenue for the current period that trailed estimates, in its first financial update since announcing it would cut about 5% of its global workforce.

title: Microsoft’s LinkedIn Chief to Run Office Group in AI Shakeup
content: The chief of Microsoft Corp.’s LinkedIn is taking charge of the teams that build email and productivity apps, in a reorganization that consolidates more of the company’s workplace software as it seeks to speed up deployment of artificial intelligence tools.

title: Pornhub Suspends Site in France to Protest Age Verification Law
content: The parent company of Pornhub, Youporn and RedTube blocked access to its adult content in France to protest new age verification requirements in the country.

title: Google Warns Hackers Stealing Salesforce Data From Companies
content: A hacking group has been impersonating IT personnel to break into companies’ Salesforce tools, using the access for data theft and extortion, according to a new report from Google’s threat intelligence group.

title: Spain Makes First Payment in Lengthy Renewable Energy Fight
content: The Spanish government made its first payment as a result of an arbitration decision in 2021 around the country’s move to change investor incentives tied to renewable energy projects, following a number of lengthy legal battles between Spain and various creditors.

title: Data Error Pushed Up UK Inflation in April, Stats Office Says
content: Britain’s statistics office has said April’s inflation number was 0.1 percentage point higher than it should have been due to an error in data provided by the Department for Transport.

title: Sweden’s Core Inflation Slowdown Backs June Rate Cut
content: Sweden’s underlying inflation rate fell to a five-month low, broadly in line with expectations and strengthening the case for the Riksbank to reduce interest rates later this month.

title: Vietnam Sends Trade Demand Reply as US Turns Up China Heat
content: Vietnam said it is responding to US demands with “goodwill” and has sent a written reply to US trade requests after the Trump administration vowed to keep pressuring the Southeast Asian nation to reduce its role in China supply chains.

content: Australia’s household spending remained tepid in April as consumers directed their spare cash to services like eating out rather than goods such as clothing and cars.

title: China’s Power Prices Nosedive in Relief to Tariff-Hit Factories
content: A crash in Chinese coal prices, and a flood of clean energy, are cutting power rates in major industrial hubs, easing pressure on some of the factories caught in the crossfire of trade hostilities with the US.

title: The TACO Trade Will Explode in July
content: Donald Trump has proven to be a lot more malleable than many in the financial world initially anticipated. Equity markets have adapted well, and now trade on the theme that Trump always chickens out (or TACO for short). That helped the S&P 500 gain 7% last month. But will this last? And will Trump capitulate again when the 90-day reciprocal tariff deadline comes?

title: Republican Tax Bill Adds $2.4 Trillion to US Deficits, CBO Says
content: The House-passed version of President Donald Trump’s tax and spending bill would add $2.42 trillion to US budget deficits over the next decade, according to a new estimate from the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office.

title: Weak US Services Activity, ADP Hiring Signal Some Tariff Strain
content: Activity at US service providers unexpectedly contracted last month for the first time in nearly a year and companies throttled back hiring, indicating the grip on the economy from higher tariffs is getting tighter.

title: CBO Projects Trump Tariffs to Cut Budget Gap by $2.8 Trillion
content: President Donald Trump’s tariff policies in effect as of mid-May would help to shrink US fiscal deficits by an estimated $2.8 trillion, according to the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office.

title: Fintech Wise Plans to Shift Main Listing From London to US
content: Wise Plc is planning to list its shares in the US, the latest blow to London’s stock market.

title: China’s Global Income Tax Crackdown Expands Beyond Ultra Rich
content: China is intensifying efforts to collect taxes on citizens’ overseas income, expanding its scrutiny to less wealthy individuals after targeting the ultra-rich last year, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Job of Last Resort Puts Further Strain on Malaysia’s Palm Sector
content: Malaysia’s palm oil industry is grappling with a dwindling labor pool as workers increasingly shun physically demanding jobs at plantations, a trend that threatens to exacerbate production woes in the major grower.

title: Citi to Cut 3,500 Tech Jobs in China as Part of Global Revamp
content: Citigroup Inc. will cut its technology employee workforce in China by about 3,500 as part of its global simplification efforts, while reiterating its commitment to the world’s second-largest economy.

title: Ram Brings Back Hemi V8 Engine in Bid to Reclaim Lost Sales
content: Ram is putting the Hemi V8 engine back in its light-duty pickup trucks, part of a blitz of changes from brand head Tim Kuniskis to claw back lost share in the hyper-competitive US truck market.

title: Even ‘White Lotus’ Buzz Isn’t Reviving Thailand’s Tourism Slump
content: Thailand’s tourism outlook in such doldrums that even the so-called The White Lotus effect — a temporary boost in Western visitors inspired by the latest Koh Samui—set season of HBO’s hit show — hasn’t been enough to offset a slump in arrivals from neighboring countries.

title: Enterprise Products Says US Set to Deny Its China Ethane Export License
content: Enterprise Products Partners LP received a notice saying the US intends to deny licenses for three proposed cargoes of ethane heading to China as the Trump administration doubles down on security for exports to the country.

title: Citi Taps McLean as Australia ECM Head After Jahrling Exits
content: Citigroup Inc. appointed John McLean as its new head of equity capital markets for Australia and New Zealand, replacing Rob Jahrling, who is leaving the bank.

title: China’s Power Prices Nosedive in Relief to Tariff-Hit Factories
content: A crash in Chinese coal prices, and a flood of clean energy, are cutting power rates in major industrial hubs, easing pressure on some of the factories caught in the crossfire of trade hostilities with the US.

title: Mangione Wrote United Health Executive ‘Had It Coming,’ DA Says

title: ADHD Feels Like It’s Everywhere? Researchers See No Upswell
content: ADHD may seem like it’s everywhere at the moment, but researchers found its prevalence hasn’t changed much in recent years.

title: Judge Blocks Deportation of Colorado Attack Suspect’s Family

title: Itochu to Support Pharma Firms Entering Japan to Fill Drug Needs

title: Former Trump NASA Nominee Suggests Ties to Musk Caused His Ouster

title: China’s First Foreign-Owned Hospital Seeks More Medical Tourists

title: FDA to Meet Drug Approval Goals Despite Cuts, Commissioner Says

title: Starbucks Reshuffles Leadership to Accelerate Turnaround Bid

title: Mercedes, BMW Step Up Response to China Export Curbs to Avoid Shortages

title: Santander Names Preto as New Accounting Head Amid Broedel Saga

content: CoinFlip, an operator of a global network Bitcoin ATMs, is in the early stages of weighing a sale as dealmaking in the cryptocurrency space heats up, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Uber Mulls Using Stablecoins to Reduce Currency Costs
content: Uber Technologies Inc. is in the “study phase” of using stablecoins as a way to transfer money globally, Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi said.

title: Lutnick Urges Tougher Enforcement of Export Curbs on China
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick called for stepped up enforcement of US export controls to prevent China from stealing critical American technologies that could support Beijing’s ambitions in areas like artificial intelligence and aviation.

title: Anysphere, Hailed as Fastest Growing Startup Ever, Raises $900 Million
content: The artificial intelligence rush has enabled some small startups to grow very big very quickly. But by some estimates, none have grown as fast as Anysphere Inc., maker of the popular AI coding assistant Cursor, which has surpassed $500 million in annualized revenue, the company said.

title: German Industrial Production and Exports Declined in April
content: German industrial production and exports sank in April, dashing hopes of a cyclical recovery of the country’s critical sector amid looming US trade tariff threats.

title: Halifax Data Casts Doubt on UK House Price Resilience
content: UK house prices suffered a setback in May, according to one of the country’s biggest lenders, suggesting a patchy performance for the property market since the expiration of a tax cut for buyers.

title: India’s Central Bank Surprises With Big Rate Cut, Cash Boost
content: India’s central bank cut interest rates more than projected and unexpectedly reduced the cash reserve ratio for banks, providing a major liquidity boost to the economy as growth prospects dim and inflation subsides.

title: ECB’s Muller Sees Cuts Near End as Villeroy Hails ‘Victory’
content: The European Central Bank is approaching the end of its interest-rate cuts, according to Governing Council member Madis Muller, as another colleague declared that inflation has been vanquished.

title: Hungary’s Retail Sales Rebound Counters Industry Output Decline
content: Hungary’s retail sales surged at the start of the second quarter, making shoppers Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s bet to avoid another recession less than a year before elections.

title: Taiwan Money-Market Rate Slump May Delay Central Bank Easing
content: A surge in the Taiwanese dollar last month spurred an influx of funds, driving local money-market rates to the lowest level in more than a year and potentially delaying monetary easing by the central bank.

title: SNB Denies FX Manipulation After US Treasury Puts Swiss on List
content: The Swiss National Bank denied being a currency manipulator after the US Treasury added Switzerland to a list of economies it is closely monitoring over foreign-exchange practices.

title: US Treasury Calls on BOJ to Hike Rates to Correct Yen Weakness
content: The US Treasury called on the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates to strengthen the yen, stepping much deeper into policy recommendations for Tokyo than before in its semiannual currency report.

title: Trump’s  $12 Billion Tourism Wipeout
content: Four months into the president’s second term, his policies are upending tourism worldwide.

title: Starmer's Stock-Market Apathy Is Bad for Growth
content: It’s been another bad week for London’s status as a listing venue. A shame, then, that recent government policy has focused on private markets investing.

title: Poland’s Kotecki Says MPC Is Turning Cautious on Further Easing
content: Polish policymakers are turning increasingly cautious toward further interest-rate cuts due to growing political instability and concern over a bloated budget, central banker Ludwik Kotecki said.

title: Portugal Considers Sweetening Incentives for Golden Visa Program
content: Less than two months after Spain scrapped its golden visa due to concerns about its effect on the housing market, Portugal is considering whether to sweeten its golden visa program and make a special tax regime for expatriates even more attractive.

title: Japan, US Start Tariff Talks Amid Reports on Cars, Rare Earths
content: Japan and the US have begun the latest round of trade negotiations, with media reports suggesting Tokyo’s delegation is trying to win a reprieve from the tariffs by pledging to make more cars in the US and enhancing cooperation on rare earths.

title: Economists Slash Singapore GDP, CPI Growth Forecasts on Tariffs
content: Economists have cut growth forecasts for Singapore’s gross domestic product and consumer prices as uncertainties of the global trade war leave the Lion City vulnerable to risks.

title: Russia on Cusp of First Rate Cut Since 2022 as Inflation Eases
content: Russia’s central bank is on the cusp of the first interest-rate cut in three years, as easing inflation opens the door to relief for an economy struggling under the weight of high borrowing costs.

title: South Korea to Keep Discussing Forex With US After Currency List
content: South Korea will continue to discuss its foreign exchange policy with the US to promote mutual understanding, after the Treasury kept the Asian ally on its watchlist and called for curbing currency intervention.

title: Trump and Carney in Talks on Trade Ahead of G-7 Summit
content: US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney have been in direct contact trying to reach a trade deal, but the two sides still have work to do to find agreement, according to people familiar with the discussions.

title: Japan’s Early May Exports Drop as Tariff War Upends Commerce
content: Japan’s exports fell in the first 20 days of May as the Trump administration’s sweeping tariffs continued to disrupt trade.

title: Japan’s Household Spending Falls in Blow for Shrinking Economy
content: Japan’s household spending unexpectedly declined in April as elevated inflation deterred discretionary spending, in a worrisome sign for policymakers after the economy began contracting even before US tariff measures fully kicked in.

title: Bond Traders Look to US Jobs Report for Signals of Fed Rate Path
content: Bond traders will dissect the May jobs report for any signs of a softening labor market as they gauge the timing of Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts.

title: US Companies Likely Held Onto Workers in May Despite Tariff Uncertainty
content: US hiring likely moderated further in May and the unemployment rate was little changed, suggesting employers are yet to implement big changes to their headcount in response to President Donald Trump’s trade policy.

title: US Deficit Is a ‘Ticking Time Bomb,’ Citadel Securities President Says

title: Candidate for Bank of Thailand Chief Backs Aggressive Rate Cuts
content: Thailand should be more aggressive in cutting borrowing costs given its bleak growth outlook and subdued inflation, according to Somprawin Manprasert, one of the candidates seeking to become the Bank of Thailand’s new governor.

title: Lagarde Steels for Battles Ahead After ECB Hits Sweet Spot

title: Lagarde Determined to Finish ECB Term After WEF Speculation

title: Businesses Expect to Pass Along 50% of Tariffs, Fed Survey Finds

title: Chile’s Leftist Presidential Hopefuls Open Door to Higher Taxes

title: Broadcom Falls After Lukewarm Forecast Disappoints AI Bulls

title: Dronemaker Destinus Seek Funds at Unicorn Valuation
